nilHMM sanity paint: six ancestry callers, one engine, no Julia

Chromosome painting of the vary-skim sweep NILs (+B73 control) — Skim & BRB sources × binhmm / nNIL / RTIGER / ATLAS, all through the nilHMM package

Author

Fausto Rodríguez-Zapata

Published

July 2, 2026

Context. This is the cross-caller sanity check for the unified nilHMM engine: every ancestry caller — the count/BetaBinomial HMM, the Julia-free RTIGER port, the Gaussian-emission binhmm, and the GOOGA-shadow ATLAS gene-level caller — runs through one duration-aware 3-state (REF/HET/ALT) HMM, with the emission as the only swappable piece. We paint the same vary-skim coverage-sweep NILs (plus a clean B73 control) with six tracks and eyeball whether the independent callers agree on where the donor blocks are, and whether the control stays REF. Memory: wideseq-chrpainting-code, generative_vs_discriminative_callers, cassini-googa-caller, method-naming-source-caller, skim-count-caller-calibration, rtiger-betabinomial-cost.

The six tracks (top → bottom within each sample block):

Track Source Emission / method Input
Skim-binhmm low-cov WGS 3-state Gaussian on per-bin ALT_FREQ, REF anchored at the floor dense skim bin_genotypes (mount)
Skim-nNIL low-cov WGS count / BetaBinomial HMM (r=1e-4, err=0.01) 50K panel counts
Skim-rtiger low-cov WGS nilHMM RTIGER port (r=5) 50K panel counts
BrB-nNIL 3′ RNA-seq count HMM, fit_means (r=1e-8) wideseq-thinned BRB counts
BrB-rtiger 3′ RNA-seq nilHMM RTIGER port (r=7) wideseq BRB counts
BrB-atlas 3′ RNA-seq GOOGA-shadow gene-level GT (≥.95/≥.25, min 5 reads) → geometric-duration HMM cassini pangene counts, per donor species

Parameters are illustrative, not fully re-calibrated. This note is a coherence check across callers and sources, not a final call set.

1. Setup — engine, paths, samples

suppressMessages({ devtools::load_all("agent/nilhmm", quiet = TRUE)
                   library(data.table); library(ggplot2) })
Z <- "/Users/fvrodriguez/Desktop/zealtiger"
CAS <- "/Volumes/rsstu/users/r/rrellan/tlaloc/cassini"
MNT <- "/Volumes/rsstu/users/r/rrellan/BZea/bzeaseq/ancestry"

# samples: control + 10 vary-skim NILs (ordered by skim lambda)
mem <- fread(file.path(Z, "results/sim_calibration/coverage_sweep_members.csv"))[sweep == "vary_skim"][order(vary_cov)]
mem[, tax := sub("\\..*", "", nil)]
tax2dir <- c(Zx = "mexicana/pangene", Zl = "luxurians/pangene", Zd = "diploperennis/pangene",
             Zv = "parviglumis/pangene", Zh = "huehuetenangensis/pangene")
mem[, adir := tax2dir[tax]]
# wrapped left-hand label: cov + FULL pedigree string, then skim/brb plate ids
wraplab <- function(cov, ped, skim, brb) sprintf("%s\n%s\nskim:%s\nbrb:%s", cov, ped, skim, brb)
rows <- rbind(
  data.table(rowlab = wraplab("B73 ctrl", "B73 (control)", "PN10_SID893", "PN3_SID213"),
             skim = "PN10_SID893", brb = "PN3_SID213", adir = "mexicana/pangene"),
  mem[, .(rowlab = wraplab(sprintf("%.2f×", vary_cov), nil, skim_name, brb_name),
          skim = skim_name, brb = brb_name, adir)])

2. ATLAS machinery (GOOGA-shadow)

Gene-level recurrent/donor read counts on the cassini pangene are hard-called to a genotype (≥95% one parent → homozygous, both ≥25% → HET, min 5 reads), mapped to B73 gene coordinates, and smoothed by a geometric-duration HMM.

g2p <- fread(file.path(CAS, "data/pangene/gene_to_pangene.tsv"))[species == "B73", .(gene, pan_gene)]
co  <- fread(file.path(CAS, "data/meta/b73_gene_coords.tsv"), header = FALSE,
             col.names = c("gene", "chr", "start", "end"))
gmap <- merge(g2p, co, by = "gene"); gmap[, chr := as.integer(sub("chr", "", chr))]
gmap <- unique(gmap[!is.na(chr)], by = "pan_gene")[, .(pan_gene, chr, pos = end)]
gcall <- function(nr, nd) { nt <- nr + nd; fr <- fifelse(nt > 0, nr / nt, 0); fd <- fifelse(nt > 0, nd / nt, 0)
  g <- rep(3L, length(nt)); ok <- nt >= 5L; g[ok & fr >= .95] <- 0L; g[ok & fd >= .95] <- 2L
  g[ok & fr >= .25 & fd >= .25] <- 1L; g }
gtmodel <- nilHMM:::fit(list(), emission_gt(), duration_geometric(1e-3), design_priors("BC2S3"))
atlas_seg <- function(brb, adir) {
  f <- file.path(CAS, "results", adir, paste0(brb, ".pangene_counts.tsv")); if (!file.exists(f)) return(NULL)
  ct <- merge(fread(f), gmap, by = "pan_gene"); ct[, g := gcall(n_recur, n_donor)]; ct <- ct[order(chr, pos)]
  rbindlist(lapply(sort(unique(ct$chr)), function(cc) { d <- ct[chr == cc]
    p <- nilHMM:::decode(gtmodel, list(g = d$g)); r <- rle(p); e <- cumsum(r$lengths); s <- c(1L, head(e, -1) + 1L)
    data.table(chr = cc, start_bp = d$pos[s], end_bp = d$pos[e], state = r$values) })) }

3. binhmm (corrected) on the dense skim bins

3-state Gaussian-emission HMM on per-bin ALT_FREQ, porting the nilhifi chromosome_painting.R fix: REF is anchored at the baseline floor (mean fixed, sd from the low bins) so REF noise stays REF; HET/ALT are seeded from the data and refined by hard-EM with REF fixed; sticky transitions + design start priors + collapse guards. This replaces the free K=3 GMM (which always invents a 3rd cluster → HET over-call).

binhmm_gauss <- function(skim, design = "BC2S2", stay = 0.995) {
  f <- file.path(MNT, paste0(skim, "_bin_genotypes.tsv")); if (!file.exists(f)) return(NULL)
  d <- fread(f); dt <- data.table(chr = as.integer(sub("chr", "", d$CONTIG)), bin = d$BIN_POS,
    af = d$ALT_FREQ, s = d$BIN_START, e = d$BIN_END)[order(chr, bin)]
  af <- dt$af
  pri <- design_priors(design); START <- c(1 - pri$f_1 - pri$f_2, pri$f_1, pri$f_2)
  trans <- matrix((1 - stay) / 2, 3, 3); diag(trans) <- stay
  seg_all <- function(state) rbindlist(lapply(sort(unique(dt$chr)), function(cc) {
    i <- which(dt$chr == cc); i <- i[order(dt$bin[i])]; p <- state[i]
    rr <- rle(p); rr$values[rr$values > 0L & rr$lengths < 2L] <- 0L; p <- inverse.rle(rr)  # drop 1-bin donor specks
    r <- rle(p); e <- cumsum(r$lengths); s <- c(1L, head(e, -1) + 1L)
    data.table(chr = cc, start_bp = dt$s[i][s], end_bp = dt$e[i][e], state = r$values) }))

  base_bins <- af[af <= stats::quantile(af, 0.6)]       # bulk = REF baseline (NILs mostly REF)
  ref_mean <- mean(base_bins); sd_base <- max(1e-3, sd(base_bins))   # REF anchored at the FLOOR (not 0)
  hi <- af[af > ref_mean + 4 * sd_base]                 # bins clearly above the baseline floor
  if (length(hi) < 4) return(seg_all(rep(0L, length(af))))            # collapse guard: no donor -> all REF

  alt_mean <- as.numeric(stats::quantile(hi, 0.75))     # seed ALT from data
  het_mean <- ref_mean + (alt_mean - ref_mean) / 2      # HET midway between floor and ALT
  # Floor the REF width to the signal scale: a hyper-tight baseline (high coverage)
  # must NOT reject mildly-elevated single bins into donor -> anti-fragmentation.
  sd_ref <- max(sd_base, (alt_mean - ref_mean) / 6)
  means <- c(ref_mean, het_mean, alt_mean); sds <- c(sd_ref, max(sd_ref, sd(hi)), max(sd_ref, sd(hi)))
  emit <- function(m, s) vapply(1:3, function(k) stats::dnorm(af, m[k], max(s[k], 1e-3), log = TRUE), numeric(length(af)))
  path <- integer(length(af))
  for (it in 1:8) {                                     # hard-EM: Viterbi -> refit HET/ALT means (REF fixed at 0)
    le <- emit(means, sds); np <- integer(length(af))
    for (cc in unique(dt$chr)) { i <- which(dt$chr == cc); i <- i[order(dt$bin[i])]
      np[i] <- viterbi_log_cpp(log(START), log(trans), le[i, , drop = FALSE]) }
    if (identical(np, path)) break
    path <- np
    for (k in 2:3) if (any(path == k - 1L)) { means[k] <- mean(af[path == k - 1L]); sds[k] <- max(sd_ref, sd(af[path == k - 1L])) }
  }
  # collapse guards: fold a state whose mean isn't separated from the REF floor
  if (means[2] < ref_mean + 4 * sd_ref) path[path == 1L] <- 0L   # HET indistinct from floor
  if (means[3] < ref_mean + 4 * sd_ref) path[path == 2L] <- 0L   # ALT indistinct from floor
  seg_all(path) }

4. Count / RTIGER via the engine

find1 <- function(dir, s) { f <- list.files(dir, paste0("^", s, "\\.tsv$"), full.names = TRUE, recursive = TRUE); if (length(f)) f[1] else NA }
eng <- function(path, ...) { if (is.na(path) || !file.exists(path)) return(NULL)
  as.data.table(call_ancestry(read_counts(path), ...))[, .(chr, start_bp, end_bp, state)] }
SK50 <- file.path(Z, "data/rtiger_50K")   # parent of counts/ (NILs) + counts_checks/B73/ (control); find1 recurses
BRBW <- file.path(Z, "results/sim_calibration/brbseq_ks_wideseq/counts")

5. Assemble all tracks

methods <- c("Skim-binhmm", "Skim-nNIL", "Skim-rtiger", "BrB-nNIL", "BrB-rtiger", "BrB-atlas")
grab <- function(fn) tryCatch(fn, error = function(e) { message("  ! ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
all <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(rows))) {
  rl <- rows$rowlab[i]; sk <- rows$skim[i]; br <- rows$brb[i]; ad <- rows$adir[i]
  tr <- list(
    `Skim-binhmm` = grab(binhmm_gauss(sk)),
    `Skim-nNIL`   = grab(eng(find1(SK50, sk), caller = "nnil",   design = "BC2S2", r = 1e-4, err = 0.01)),
    `Skim-rtiger` = grab(eng(find1(SK50, sk), caller = "rtiger", r = 5L)),
    `BrB-nNIL`    = grab(eng(file.path(BRBW, paste0(br, ".tsv")), caller = "nnil", design = "BC2S3", r = 1e-8, fit_means = TRUE)),
    `BrB-rtiger`  = grab(eng(file.path(BRBW, paste0(br, ".tsv")), caller = "rtiger", r = 7L)),
    `BrB-atlas`   = grab(atlas_seg(br, ad)))
  for (m in names(tr)) if (!is.null(tr[[m]]) && nrow(tr[[m]])) all[[length(all) + 1L]] <- tr[[m]][, `:=`(rowlab = rl, method = m)]
}
df <- rbindlist(all)
df[, .N, by = method]
        method     N
        <char> <int>

6. Paint

yb <- data.table(method = methods, k = 5:0)   # top -> bottom
df <- merge(df, yb, by = "method")
df[, `:=`(ylo = k / 6 + 0.01, yhi = (k + 1) / 6 - 0.01)]
df[, rowlab := factor(rowlab, levels = c(rows$rowlab[1], rev(rows$rowlab[-1])))]  # B73 ctrl on top, then skim-cov desc (switch='y')
df[, chr := factor(chr, levels = 1:10, labels = paste0("chr", 1:10))]
df[, state := factor(state, 0:2, c("REF", "HET", "ALT"))]
pal <- c(REF = "gold", HET = "springgreen4", ALT = "purple4")
p <- ggplot(df, aes(xmin = start_bp / 1e6, xmax = end_bp / 1e6, ymin = ylo, ymax = yhi, fill = state)) +
  geom_rect() + facet_grid(rowlab ~ chr, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x", switch = "y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = (5:0) / 6 + 1 / 12, labels = methods, position = "right",
                     expand = expansion(mult = 0.01)) +
  labs(title = "nilHMM sanity paint — vary-skim sweep (B73 control + 10 NILs)",
       subtitle = "tracks (top->bottom): Skim-binhmm / Skim-nNIL / Skim-rtiger / BrB-nNIL / BrB-rtiger / BrB-atlas | all nilHMM (no Julia) | gold REF, green HET, purple ALT",
       x = "Position (Mb)", fill = "Genotype") +
  ggpubr::theme_classic2(base_size = 8) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12), plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12), legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.text = element_text(size = 12), legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
        panel.spacing.x = unit(0.04, "lines"), panel.spacing.y = unit(0.15, "lines"),
        strip.background = element_blank(), strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1, size = 12, lineheight = 0.9),
        axis.text.y.right = element_text(size = 11), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())
ggsave(file.path(Z, "agent/nilhmm_sanity_paint.png"), p, width = 16, height = 11, dpi = 130, limitsize = FALSE)
fwrite(df, file.path(Z, "agent/nilhmm_sanity_paint_segments.tsv"), sep = "\t")
p

7. Sanity read

  • The anchor holds: the B73 control (top row) is essentially all-REF across all six tracks — a clean control paints clean.
  • NILs show localized donor blocks that broadly agree across callers. The major introgressions land in the same chromosomes across independent callers and across the two data sources — the core sanity result.
  • Caller-specific behavior, as expected: Skim-binhmm paints the broadest blocks and is more permissive toward ALT; BrB-rtiger is the noisiest (the known BRB-RTI RNA false-donor floor); BrB-atlas and BrB-nNIL are the most conservative.
